newsitem.title: USA: Insilco OKs buyback of up $220 mln in shrs.
newsitem.headline: Insilco OKs buyback of up $220 mln in shrs.

text.p: Insilco Corp said Friday that it approved the purchase of up to $220 million of its shares of common stock.
The share repurchase is taking place in two steps in order to provide a tax-efficient distribution to all shareholders, the company said.

First, on July 10, Insilco bought 2,805,194 shares from its majority shareholder, Water Street Corporate Recovery Fund I LP, and 51,948 shares from Robert Smialek, Insilco chairman and CEO, at $38.50 per share, for an aggregate purchase price of $110 million.
These purchases were financed with proceeds from the sale of Insilco's Rolodex division, completed in March, the company said.
Second, Insilco said today it commenced a $110 million self-tender offer for up to 2,857,142 shares of Insilco's outstanding shares, at $38.50 per share.
On July 10, the company said it refinanced its existing debt under a new six year $200 million credit agreement.
The offer will be financed out of borrowings under the new credit agreement and the proceeds of a potential offering of up to $150 million of new debt, the company said.

On a pro forma basis, after giving effect to the new capital structure, the completion of the share repurchases, and the acquisitions and divestitures completed in 1996 and 1997, the company's 1996 earnings per share would have been $3.89, Insilco said.

Assuming full participation in the offer, the company said it will have about 3,854,152 shares of common stock outstanding, of which Water Street will own 2,400,001 shares, or 62.3 percent of the total outstanding, as compared to its 60.6 percent ownership before these transactions.
